name: Simon of Cyrene
title: The Cross-Bearer
summary: Simon of Cyrene was a man from the North African city of Cyrene who was forced by Roman soldiers to carry Jesus' cross on the way to Golgotha. He is one of the few people mentioned by name in connection with the crucifixion, and his sons Alexander and Rufus apparently became known in the early church.

keyEvents.title: Forced to Carry the Cross
keyEvents.description: When Jesus was too exhausted to carry the cross himself, Roman soldiers forced Simon of Cyrene to carry it for him on the way to Golgotha.

keyEvents.title: Father of Alexander and Rufus
keyEvents.description: Mark mentions that Simon was the father of Alexander and Rufus, suggesting that these sons were known in the early Christian community.

keyEvents.title: Came from the Country
keyEvents.description: Simon came from the country and was on his way into Jerusalem when he was stopped and forced to carry the cross, possibly during the Passover celebration.

keyEvents.title: Possible Connection to the Church in Rome
keyEvents.description: Paul greets a Rufus and his mother in Romans, and many believe this may be Simon's son, suggesting that the family became part of the early church.
